title.en: Distinguish the Internet from the WWW

say.en: You type a website name, not a string of numbers, yet your browser finds the right server in another country. Who looked up the number for you? In this lesson: Distinguish the Internet from the WWW.
Explain HTML, URL and HTTP.
Describe IoT.
Explain DNS and name resolution.

body.en: The *Internet* is the global network of networks. The World Wide Web (WWW) is a service on the Internet: a huge collection of web pages linked by hyperlinks. It rests on three technologies: HTML to create pages, URI/URL to give each resource a unique address, and HTTP to transfer pages between servers and browsers. The Internet of Things (IoT) connects everyday devices, such as smart meters, watches, cameras and appliances, so they can collect and exchange data.

points.en: *Internet* = network of networks; WWW = service on it

narration.en: The Internet is the network of networks, and the Web is one service on it, built from HTML, URLs and HTTP. IoT connects everyday devices.

title.en: How DNS finds an IP address

narration.en: Computers reach each other by IP address, but we type names. The resolver asks a root server, which points to the .in server, which points to the domain's own name server, which gives the IP address. A cached answer skips all of that. Look up the name with no cache. How many messages travel? Turn on the cache. How much time does it save at 30 ms per hop?
narration.kn: ಕಂಪ್ಯೂಟರ್‌ಗಳು IP ವಿಳಾಸದಿಂದ ಸಂಪರ್ಕಿಸುತ್ತವೆ, ನಾವು ಹೆಸರು ಟೈಪ್ ಮಾಡುತ್ತೇವೆ. ರಿಸಾಲ್ವರ್ ಮೂಲ ಸರ್ವರ್ ಕೇಳುತ್ತದೆ, ಅದು .in ಸರ್ವರ್ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, ಅದು ಡೊಮೇನ್‌ನ ಸ್ವಂತ ಹೆಸರು ಸರ್ವರ್ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, ಅದು IP ವಿಳಾಸ ಕೊಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಕ್ಯಾಶ್ ಉತ್ತರ ಇವೆಲ್ಲವನ್ನೂ ತಪ್ಪಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಕ್ಯಾಶ್ ಇಲ್ಲದೆ ಹೆಸರು ಹುಡುಕಿ. ಎಷ್ಟು ಸಂದೇಶಗಳು ಚಲಿಸುತ್ತವೆ? ಕ್ಯಾಶ್ ಆನ್ ಮಾಡಿ. ಪ್ರತಿ ಹಾಪ್‌ಗೆ 30 ms ಆದರೆ ಎಷ್ಟು ಸಮಯ ಉಳಿತಾಯ?

title.en: On the board: How DNS finds ncert.nic.in

say.en: A domain name is read from right to left. dot in is the top-level domain, nic is the second level, ncert is the host.
Computers need the IP address. The browser asks a DNS resolver.
If the resolver does not know, it asks a root server, then the dot in server, then nic’s own name server.
The name server returns the IP address. The browser then connects to that address with HTTP.
The web rests on three ideas: HTML for pages, URLs for addresses, and HTTP to carry them.

body.en: Computers find each other by IP address, but people remember names. A domain name such as ncert.nic.in is read from right to left: .in is the top-level domain, nic is the second level. The *Domain Name System* (DNS) translates domain names into IP addresses; this is called name resolution. When you type a URL, your computer asks a DNS server; if it does not know, the query passes through root servers, top-level domain servers and the domain's own name server until the IP address is found.

heading.en: How a message travels the internet

tagline.en: Chop it into packets, hop through routers, rebuild it at the other end.

myth.en: The internet is a cloud in the sky, and a message travels through it in one piece.

truth.en: The internet is millions of computers and routers joined by real cables (even under the sea). Messages are cut into small packets that can take different roads.

say.en: Mia wants to send a photo to Grandma, far away. In between are lots of computers called routers, all joined up. That is the internet.
A big photo is cut into small pieces called packets. Each packet gets a label: who it is for, and its number, like 2 of 4.
Each router reads the label and passes the packet to a neighbour that is closer to Grandma. Hop, hop, hop!
If one router has a traffic jam, packets go around it. Some roads are longer, so the packets can arrive in a jumbled order.
Grandma's tablet reads the numbers and puts the pieces in order: 1, 2, 3, 4. The whole photo appears!

title.en: A packet got lost? Ask again!

say.en: Sometimes a packet gets lost. Grandma's tablet notices number 3 is missing and asks for it again. Mia's laptop sends a new copy.

limits.en: Real packets travel in thousandths of a second, and there can be thousands of them for one photo. Lost packets are spotted automatically using acknowledgements and timers — no one has to notice a missing piece by eye.

problem.en: Break the URL https://www.example.in/admission/form.html into its parts.

steps.en: https → protocol used to fetch the page (secure HTTP).
www.example.in → domain name; .in is the top-level domain.
/admission/form.html → path to the page on the server.
DNS converts www.example.in into the server's IP address before the page is fetched.
